## Declarations and implementations

```plato

// Elastic stiffness of a spring, stored in newtons per meter
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stiffness).
type Stiffness implements IQuantity { NewtonsPerMeter: Number; }

// Viscous damping coefficient, stored in newton-seconds per meter
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damping).
type DampingCoefficient implements IQuantity { NewtonSecondsPerMeter: Number; }

// Dynamic viscosity, stored in pascal-seconds
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscosity).
type DynamicViscosity implements IQuantity { PascalSeconds: Number; }

// Kinematic viscosity, stored in square meters per second.
type KinematicViscosity implements IQuantity { SquareMetersPerSecond: Number; }

// Mass flow, stored in kilograms per second
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_flow_rate).
type MassFlowRate implements IQuantity { KilogramsPerSecond: Number; }

// Volume flow, stored in cubic meters per second
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volumetric_flow_rate).
type VolumetricFlowRate implements IQuantity { CubicMetersPerSecond: Number; }

// Dimensionless deformation ratio (change in length over length)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strain_(mechanics)).
type Strain implements IQuantity { Ratio: Number; }

//==
// # Mechanical quantities
//
// Mass and its distributions, the force / torque / impulse family, linear and
// angular momentum with rotational inertia, and energy and power
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_mechanics). Material response
// (stress, stiffness, viscosity, flow) is the material section.

// Mass, stored in kilograms (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass).
type Mass implements IQuantity { Kilograms: Number; }

// Mass per volume, stored in kilograms per cubic meter
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Density).
type Density implements IQuantity { KilogramsPerCubicMeter: Number; }

// Mass per area, stored in kilograms per square meter
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_density).
type ArealDensity implements IQuantity { KilogramsPerSquareMeter: Number; }

// Mass per length, stored in kilograms per meter
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_density).
type LinearDensity implements IQuantity { KilogramsPerMeter: Number; }

// Force, stored in newtons (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force).
type Force implements IQuantity { Newtons: Number; }

// Rotational force, stored in newton-meters (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torque).
type Torque implements IQuantity { NewtonMeters: Number; }

// Impulse (force integrated over time), stored in newton-seconds
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impulse_(physics)).
type Impulse implements IQuantity { NewtonSeconds: Number; }

// Linear momentum, stored in kilogram-meters per second
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Momentum).
type Momentum implements IQuantity { KilogramMetersPerSecond: Number; }

// Angular momentum, stored in kilogram-square-meters per second
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_momentum).
type AngularMomentum implements IQuantity { KilogramSquareMetersPerSecond: Number; }

// Rotational inertia about an axis, stored in kilogram-square-meters
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_of_inertia).
type MomentOfInertia implements IQuantity { KilogramSquareMeters: Number; }

// Energy or work, stored in joules (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy).
type Energy implements IQuantity { Joules: Number; }

// Rate of energy transfer, stored in watts
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_(physics)).
type Power implements IQuantity { Watts: Number; }

//==
// # Photometric and radiometric quantities
//
// Light measured as the eye responds to it - intensity, flux, illuminance,
// luminance (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photometry_(optics)) - plus
// `Irradiance`, the one radiometric member here, which measures raw radiant
// power per area with no luminosity weighting.

// Luminous intensity, stored in candelas
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminous_intensity).
type LuminousIntensity implements IQuantity { Candelas: Number; }

// Luminous flux, stored in lumens
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminous_flux).
type LuminousFlux implements IQuantity { Lumens: Number; }

// Illuminance, stored in lux (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminance).
type Illuminance implements IQuantity { Lux: Number; }

// Luminance, stored in candelas per square meter (nits)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminance).
type Luminance implements IQuantity { CandelasPerSquareMeter: Number; }

// Radiant flux per area, stored in watts per square meter
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irradiance).
type Irradiance implements IQuantity { WattsPerSquareMeter: Number; }

//==
// # Thermal and chemical quantities
//
// Absolute temperature and its delta type, the two heat-transport constants,
// and amount of substance (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamics).
// `Temperature` is an absolute (kelvin) reading and `TemperatureDelta` is the
// difference between two of them - they share a unit but not a meaning, so a
// delta is never a temperature.

// Absolute temperature, stored in kelvin
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_temperature).
type Temperature implements IQuantity { Kelvin: Number; }

// Temperature difference, stored in kelvin.
type TemperatureDelta implements IQuantity { Kelvin: Number; }

// Heat capacity, stored in joules per kelvin
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_capacity).
type HeatCapacity implements IQuantity { JoulesPerKelvin: Number; }

// Thermal conductivity, stored in watts per meter-kelvin
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermal_conductivity_and_resistivity).
type ThermalConductivity implements IQuantity { WattsPerMeterKelvin: Number; }

// Amount of substance, stored in moles
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amount_of_substance).
type AmountOfSubstance implements IQuantity { Moles: Number; }
```
